# Interim Exploitation of German and Austrian Specialists under Project Paperclip — FRUS1946V, document448

## Bibliographic identity and selected witness

Office of the Historian, Foreign Relations of the United States,1946, The British Commonwealth, Western and Central Europe, volumeV, document448, file862.542/9–346. The cover is Dean Acheson’s top-secret memorandum as Acting Secretary of State to President Truman, Washington,30August1946. The enclosure states interim policy. Editorial note89 records the handwritten approval dated3September1946. The selected object is the institutional HTML transcription, not a newly collated original signed memorandum.

## Reading scope and consumption

Cover memorandum, enclosure2a–b and editorial approval note89; navigation excluded. No complete personnel archive or compliance audit. Full named scope was read in the T21 law development; the text hash matches the later T22 consumer-source receipt. This admission reuses that reading and rechecks the exact passages, not a new whole-book or archival investigation. No direct quotation is admitted.

The [language–law–nation history](../../../../histories/places-and-peoples/language-law-nation-centralisation/DEVELOPMENT.md#branch-xi-postwar) consumes the bounded witness in its existing situated branch. Historical claim, legal prescription, authorial comparison and implementation evidence retain separate standing.

<a id="us-1946-paperclip-policy-frus448-q001"></a>
## Passage card — `us-1946-paperclip-policy-frus448-q001` — Cover, expansion and approval
^us-1946-paperclip-policy-frus448-q001

> **Paraphrase (not a quotation):** Acheson recommends expanding the existing Paperclip programme to secure the services of German and Austrian specialists, with family movement, modified custody and possible later immigration status. The cover identifies agreement among State, War and Navy. The editorial approval note identifies Truman’s3September approval. Recommendation, approved policy and a particular person’s later appointment are distinct objects.

- **Locator:** Document448, cover memorandum30August1946 and editorial note89 recording approval3September1946.
- **Status:** paraphrase-only.
- **Source relation:** Paraphrased.
- **Verification:** exact named scope read in the prior law packet; saved witness and extraction hashes rebound2026-09-08.
- **Provenance:** institutional witness and immutable local-copy hashes above.

<a id="us-1946-paperclip-policy-frus448-q002"></a>
## Passage card — `us-1946-paperclip-policy-frus448-q002` — Contract, custody and screening rules
^us-1946-paperclip-policy-frus448-q002

> **Paraphrase (not a quotation):** The enclosure prescribes contracts, movement of specialists and families, temporary limited military custody, return where necessary and biographical/security records. Clause2a(5) excludes more-than-nominal Nazi Party participation or active support for Nazism or militarism. Scientific or technical honours alone do not disqualify a specialist; doubtful cases may receive further screening in the United States. Clause2b distributes continuing information and screening duties. These are stated rules, not evidence that screening or every appointment complied.

- **Locator:** Document448, enclosure2a(1)–(7) and2b(1)–(3); internal page marker691 falls within2a(6).
